name: Jim Risch

issue_poll.name: Mountain States Policy Center 2026 Idaho Poll (RMG Research, 600 Idaho registered voters, Jan 2-9, 2026; most important issue) combined with Pew Research Center national survey of registered voters, Sept. 28-Oct. 4, 2026 (share calling each issue 'very important')
issue_poll.note: Combined. The only 2026 Idaho poll found that ranks issues is the MSPC Idaho Poll, which published only its top three (economy 31%, taxes 19%, education 18%); these are ranks 1-3. Ranks 4-10 are the next Pew national items in Pew order (https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2026/10/08/economy-ranks-as-top-issue-in-midterms-for-all-voters-but-partisans-differ-over-the-importance-of-other-issues/): future of democracy 73, health care 68, immigration 59, foreign policy 57, energy 54, violent crime 52, abortion 46 (economy and education already placed). No 2026 Idaho Senate-race poll (Bullfinch, Change Research, Peak Insights, ATR, VoteNexus, PPP) published an issue question. Boise State's 2026 Idaho Public Policy Survey (Nov 2025) asked only state-budget priorities (housing 39%, K-12 education 26%, tax relief 15%, transportation 12%), so it was not used for ranking; housing is folded into Economy. Public lands (96% want them kept public) and wildfire (53% extremely/very serious, State of the Rockies Jan 2026) are salient in Idaho but no comparable importance measure was found, so they were not slotted.

issues.detail: Increase domestic oil, gas, nuclear and geothermal production to lower prices; rein in federal spending; end Iran war to lower prices
Repeal the federal estate tax; further tax cuts
Stand up for fairness in girls' sports
Pass the SAVE Act requiring documentary proof of citizenship to register to vote
Replace the Affordable Care Act rather than reform it; shift health care substantially toward the private sector
Allow H-2A agricultural visas for year-round work (e.g. dairy); oppose any path to citizenship for those who entered illegally
Support Trump tariffs; Columbia River Treaty renegotiation must protect Idaho water rights; bring Iran war to a close
Oppose breaching the four lower Snake River dams; oppose wind projects like Lava Ridge; expand nuclear and small modular reactors at Idaho National Laboratory
Campaign site touts pro-life group ratings (SBA Pro-Life America A+); no stated position

plan_caveats: Issue ranking combines a January 2026 Idaho poll (top three only published) with national Pew ranks for 4-10; no fall 2026 Idaho poll asked an issue question.

Risch's campaign issues page (senatorrisch.com/issues) could not be fetched; positions come from his 2026 KBOI/idahonews candidate survey, his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, Idaho Capital Sun interview reporting (Aug 2026) and Spokesman-Review/KIFI reporting (Oct 2026). The Idaho Capital Sun Sept 30, 2026 candidate Q&A on tariffs, Iran and spending could not be fetched.
No debate was held; Risch did not accept Achilles's debate challenge as far as found.

Taxes rated Concrete on estate-tax repeal, which Risch listed in his 2026 candidate survey among bills he backs to help farmers and ranchers; it is a past-sponsored bill restated as a campaign position. The Working Families Tax Cut Act (no tax on tips/overtime/Social Security) is already law and was treated as record.
Immigration rated Concrete on year-round H-2A eligibility, which Risch said he supports (the Idaho dairy industry's ask); the path-to-citizenship item is opposition only.
Energy rated Concrete on opposing Snake River dam breaching (clear end state); Lava Ridge cancellation is record.
Health care rated Partial: 'replace ACA' is from reporter paraphrase of an interview and no replacement was described.
Education rated Vague: the girls' sports line is a campaign-site slogan reported by an aggregator; no school-policy commitment found. The whole-milk-in-schools law he cited is already enacted.
Abortion rated Vague (not None) because the campaign site highlights pro-life ratings, matching how an SBA endorsement was treated in other plans; no 2026 abortion statement was found.
Housing: he points to the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, already law (pointing to existing law), folded into Economy.
Ballotpedia result: Risch 56.0%, Achilles (I) 34.3%, Fleming (I) 6.9%, Loesby (L) 2.9% (uncertified).
